grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.titleTraditional: 想起來：想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來
grammarPages.titleEnglish: Now Remember / Can or Can’t Remember
grammarPages.explanation: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “想起來” is used when someone suddenly remembers something that is almost forgotten or recalls something with great effort. “想得起來／想不起來” indicates whether or not someone can remember something almost forgotten or happened a long time ago.
grammarPages.pattern: 想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來

text.traditional: 太太：你怎麼看起來這麼緊張啊？先生：我忽然想起來今天要開會，我得快點兒去公司！
text.simplified: 太太：你怎么看起来这么紧张啊？先生：我忽然想起来今天要开会，我得快点儿去公司！
text.pinyin: Tàitai: Nǐ zěnme kànqǐlái zhème jǐnzhāng a? Xiānshēng: Wǒ hūrán xiǎng qǐlái jīntiān yào kāihuì, wǒ děi kuài diǎnr qù gōngsī!
text.english: Wife: Why do you look so nervous? Husband: I suddenly remembered that I have a meeting today. I have to hurry to the office!

text.traditional: A：你記得我們上次去的 KTV 在哪裡嗎？B：我想想……想起來了！就在捷運龍山寺站的附近。
text.simplified: A：你记得我们上次去的 KTV 在哪里吗？B：我想想……想起来了！就在捷运龙山寺站的附近。
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ jìde wǒmen shàng cì qù de KTV zài nǎlǐ ma? B: Wǒ xiǎng xiǎng… xiǎng qǐlái le! Jiù zài Jiéyùn Lóngshān Sì Zhàn de fùjìn.
text.english: A: Do you remember where the KTV we went to last time is? B: Let me think… I remember now! It’s right near Longshan Temple MRT Station.

text.traditional: A：我是你的小學同學，你還記得我的名字嗎？B：你叫……對不起，我想不起來了。
text.simplified: A：我是你的小学同学，你还记得我的名字吗？B：你叫……对不起，我想不起来了。
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ shì nǐ de xiǎoxué tóngxué, nǐ hái jìde wǒ de míngzi ma? B: Nǐ jiào… duìbùqǐ, wǒ xiǎng bù qǐlái le.
text.english: A: I am your elementary school classmate. Do you still remember my name? B: Your name is… Sorry, I can’t remember.

text.traditional: A：你小時候第一次看的卡通是什麼，你想得起來嗎？B：那麼久以前的事，我怎麼想得起來！
text.simplified: A：你小时候第一次看的卡通是什么，你想得起来吗？B：那么久以前的事，我怎么想得起来！
text.pinyin: A: Nǐ xiǎoshíhòu dì yī cì kàn de kǎtōng shì shénme, nǐ xiǎng de qǐlái ma? B: Nàme jiǔ yǐqián de shì, wǒ zěnme xiǎng de qǐlái!
text.english: A: What was the first cartoon you watched as a child? Can you remember? B: How could I remember something from so long ago!

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the sentences with a suitable 想起來 form.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say what you have never done with 從來沒, or what you never do with 從來不.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern expresses that someone has never done something, or never does something.

text.traditional: A：這個週末我們一起去 KTV 唱歌，怎麼樣？B：太好了！我從來沒去過 KTV，一定很好玩。
text.simplified: A：这个周末我们一起去 KTV 唱歌，怎么样？B：太好了！我从来没去过 KTV，一定很好玩。
text.pinyin: A: Zhège zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ qù KTV chànggē, zěnmeyàng? B: Tài hǎo le! Wǒ cónglái méi qù guo KTV, yídìng hěn hǎowán.
text.english: A: How about going to KTV to sing together this weekend? B: Great! I’ve never been to KTV; it must be fun.

text.traditional: A：下班以後，我們找老王一起去健身吧！B：不用找他了，他從來不運動！
text.simplified: A：下班以后，我们找老王一起去健身吧！B：不用找他了，他从来不运动！
text.pinyin: A: Xiàbān yǐhòu, wǒmen zhǎo Lǎo Wáng yìqǐ qù jiànshēn ba! B: Búyòng zhǎo tā le, tā cónglái bú yùndòng!
text.english: A: Let’s ask Lao Wang to work out with us after work! B: There’s no need; he never exercises!

text.traditional: A：我從來沒去過阿里山，聽說那裡的日出很美，是真的嗎？B：阿里山的日出是很美，夜裡看星星也不錯喔！
text.simplified: A：我从来没去过阿里山，听说那里的日出很美，是真的吗？B：阿里山的日出是很美，夜里看星星也不错喔！
text.pinyin: A: Wǒ cónglái méi qù guo Ālǐ Shān, tīngshuō nàlǐ de rìchū hěn měi, shì zhēnde ma? B: Ālǐ Shān de rìchū shì hěn měi, yèlǐ kàn xīngxīng yě búcuò o!
text.english: A: I’ve never been to Alishan. I heard the sunrise there is beautiful. Is that true? B: The sunrise at Alishan is beautiful, and stargazing at night is nice too!

grammarPages.learnerPromise: Add 等等 after a list when more examples of the same kind are left unlisted.
grammarPages.explanation: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: Similar to “等”, “等等” is used to show there are still more items of the same kind that are not entirely listed. Normally, “等等” should not be placed after proper nouns.

text.traditional: 便利商店的貼紙，可以換尺、牙刷、卡通娃娃等等。
text.simplified: 便利商店的贴纸，可以换尺、牙刷、卡通娃娃等等。
text.pinyin: Biànlì shāngdiàn de tiēzhǐ, kěyǐ huàn chǐ, yáshuā, kǎtōng wáwa děngděng.
text.english: Convenience store stickers can be exchanged for rulers, toothbrushes, cartoon dolls, and so on.

text.traditional: 為了身體健康，薯條、漢堡、餅乾等等，最好少吃。
text.simplified: 为了身体健康，薯条、汉堡、饼干等等，最好少吃。
text.pinyin: Wèile shēntǐ jiànkāng, shǔtiáo, hànbǎo, bǐnggān děngděng, zuìhǎo shǎo chī.
text.english: For good health, it’s best to eat fewer french fries, hamburgers, cookies, and similar foods.

text.traditional: 去鄉下爺爺奶奶家的時候，我會幫他們種花、剪草等等。
text.simplified: 去乡下爷爷奶奶家的时候，我会帮他们种花、剪草等等。
text.pinyin: Qù xiāngxià yéye nǎinai jiā de shíhòu, wǒ huì bāng tāmen zhòng huā, jiǎn cǎo děngděng.
text.english: When I go to my grandparents’ home in the countryside, I help them plant flowers, cut grass, and so on.

grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the dialogues with 等等.

dialogue.title: 年年有「魚」
dialogue.setting: 在學校餐廳 · In the school canteen
grammarFocus: 想起來：想起來了／沒想起來／想得起來／想不起來

text.traditional: （在學校餐廳）
text.simplified: （在学校餐厅）
text.pinyin: (Zài xuéxiào cāntīng)
text.english: (In the school canteen.)

text.traditional: 老師對報告的要求真多，所以我的期末報告修改了好幾次，還好最後都完成了，可以開心地放寒假了！
text.simplified: 老师对报告的要求真多，所以我的期末报告修改了好几次，还好最后都完成了，可以开心地放寒假了！
text.pinyin: Lǎoshī duì bàogào de yāoqiú zhēn duō, suǒyǐ wǒ de qímò bàogào xiūgǎi le hǎojǐ cì, háihǎo zuìhòu dōu wánchéng le, kěyǐ kāixīn de fàng hánjià le!
text.english: The teacher had many requirements for our reports, so I revised my final report many times. Fortunately, I’ve got everything done at last. I can happily enjoy the winter vacation!

text.traditional: 是啊！我一回去就要幫媽媽打掃，準備過年。
text.simplified: 是啊！我一回去就要帮妈妈打扫，准备过年。
text.pinyin: Shì a! Wǒ yì huíqù jiùyào bāng māma dǎsǎo, zhǔnbèi guònián.
text.english: Right! As soon as I go back home, I will help my mom do the cleaning and prepare for the coming New Year.

text.traditional: 過年？我想起來了，是不是中國新年？
text.simplified: 过年？我想起来了，是不是中国新年？
text.pinyin: Guònián? Wǒ xiǎng qǐlái le, shì bú shì Zhōngguó xīnnián?
text.english: New Year? I remember! Is it the Chinese New Year?

text.traditional: 對，就是中國新年，也叫春節。義大利人不過年嗎？
text.simplified: 对，就是中国新年，也叫春节。义大利人不过年吗？
text.pinyin: Duì, jiùshì Zhōngguó xīnnián, yě jiào Chūnjié. Yìdàlì rén búguò nián ma?
text.english: Yes, it is exactly the Chinese New Year, also called the Spring Festival. Don’t the Italians celebrate the New Year?

text.traditional: 我們過的是一月一號的新年。十二月三十一號跨年那天，熱鬧極了。
text.simplified: 我们过的是一月一号的新年。十二月三十一号跨年那天，热闹极了。
text.pinyin: Wǒmen guò de shì yī yuè yī hào de xīnnián. Shí'èr yuè sānshí yī hào kuànián nà tiān, rènao jíle.
text.english: We celebrate it on January 1st. On December 31st, New Year’s Eve, it is extremely lively.

text.traditional: 原來是這樣。不過，你知道中國人是怎麼過年的嗎？
text.simplified: 原来是这样。不过，你知道中国人是怎么过年的吗？
text.pinyin: Yuánlái shì zhèyàng. Búguò, nǐ zhīdào Zhōngguó rén shì zěnme guònián de ma?
text.english: Oh, I see. But do you know how Chinese people celebrate the New Year?

text.traditional: 從來沒聽過……妳們給我介紹一下吧！
text.simplified: 从来没听过……你们给我介绍一下吧！
text.pinyin: Cónglái méi tīng guo… nǐ men gěi wǒ jièshào yíxià ba!
text.english: I’ve never heard about it... Please give me a short introduction!

text.traditional: 春節的前一天是「除夕」，除夕前幾天，得把房子打掃乾淨……
text.simplified: 春节的前一天是「除夕」，除夕前几天，得把房子打扫干净……
text.pinyin: Chūnjié de qián yì tiān shì “Chúxī”, chúxī qián jǐ tiān, děi bǎ fángzi dǎsǎo gānjìng…
text.english: The day before the Spring Festival is Chinese New Year’s Eve. A few days before the Chinese New Year’s Eve, we need to clean up the house…

text.traditional: （美心接著說）除夕那天下午，我們回到爺爺、奶奶家以後，要先拜拜；等拜完了祖先，家人就聚在一起吃「年夜飯」。
text.simplified: （美心接着说）除夕那天下午，我们回到爷爷、奶奶家以后，要先拜拜；等拜完了祖先，家人就聚在一起吃「年夜饭」。
text.pinyin: (Měixīn jiēzhe shuō) Chúxī nà tiān xiàwǔ, wǒmen huí dào yéye, nǎinai jiā yǐhòu, yào xiān bàibài; děng bài wán le zǔxiān, jiārén jiù jù zài yìqǐ chī “niányèfàn”.
text.english: (Continues to speak.) On the afternoon of Chinese New Year’s Eve, after we return to grandpa and grandma’s house, we worship together first. After worshiping the ancestors, the whole family gathers to eat “family reunion dinner” together.

text.traditional: 年夜飯跟平常吃的飯不一樣嗎？
text.simplified: 年夜饭跟平常吃的饭不一样吗？
text.pinyin: Niányèfàn gēn píngcháng chī de fàn bù yíyàng ma?
text.english: Is the family reunion dinner different from usual food?

text.traditional: 年夜飯特別豐富喔！我媽媽會炸年糕、煮水餃、炒米粉，還會煎一條好吃的魚，可是不能吃完。
text.simplified: 年夜饭特别丰富喔！我妈妈会炸年糕、煮水饺、炒米粉，还会煎一条好吃的鱼，可是不能吃完。
text.pinyin: Niányèfàn tèbié fēngfù o! Wǒ māma huì zhà niángāo, zhǔ shuǐjiǎo, chǎo mǐfěn, hái huì jiān yì tiáo hǎochī de yú, kěshì bùnéng chī wán.
text.english: The family reunion dinner is particularly abundant! My mom will make deep-fried glutinous rice cake, boiled dumplings, and fried rice noodles along with a delicious fried fish. However, we can’t eat up the whole fish.

text.traditional: 為什麼不能吃完？
text.simplified: 为什么不能吃完？
text.pinyin: Wèishénme bùnéng chī wán?
text.english: Why can’t you eat it up?

text.traditional: 因為要「年年有餘」，「餘」跟「魚」都唸 yú，有「剩下」的意思。如果年夜飯有剩下的魚，新的一年就會有很多食物。
text.simplified: 因为要「年年有余」，「余」跟「鱼」都念 yú，有「剩下」的意思。如果年夜饭有剩下的鱼，新的一年就会有很多食物。
text.pinyin: Yīnwèi yào “niánnián yǒuyú”, “yú” gēn “yú” dōu niàn yú, yǒu “shèngxià” de yìsi. Rúguǒ niányèfàn yǒu shèngxià de yú, xīn de yì nián jiù huì yǒu hěn duō shíwù.
text.english: Because we hope to have a prosperous new year! Both “餘” and “魚” are both pronounced as yú. It means “surplus”. If there’s some fish left during the dinner, we’ll have plenty of food in the coming new year!

text.traditional: 除了魚，像年糕、發糕、蘿蔔糕等等，也是過年會吃的食物。
text.simplified: 除了鱼，像年糕、发糕、萝卜糕等等，也是过年会吃的食物。
text.pinyin: Chúle yú, xiàng niángāo, fāgāo, luóbogāo děngděng, yě shì guònián huì chī de shíwù.
text.english: Apart from fish, things like glutinous rice cakes, sponge cakes, radish cakes, and so on are also eaten during the Chinese New Year.

text.traditional: 這些東西也有特別的意思嗎？
text.simplified: 这些东西也有特别的意思吗？
text.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi yě yǒu tèbié de yìsi ma?
text.english: Do these things have special meanings, too?

text.traditional: 有啊！年糕代表「年年高升」、發糕是「發財」的意思；吃了蘿蔔糕就會很幸運喔！
text.simplified: 有啊！年糕代表「年年高升」、发糕是「发财」的意思；吃了萝卜糕就会很幸运喔！
text.pinyin: Yǒu a! Niángāo dàibiǎo “niánnián gāoshēng”, fāgāo shì “fācái” de yìsi; chī le luóbogāo jiù huì hěn xìngyùn o!
text.english: They do! Glutinous rice cake represents getting promoted year by year, sponge cake means making a fortune, and you will be lucky when you eat the radish cake!

text.traditional: 還要準備「平平安安」的蘋果跟「大吉大利」的橘子。
text.simplified: 还要准备「平平安安」的苹果跟「大吉大利」的橘子。
text.pinyin: Háiyào zhǔnbèi “píngpíng ān'ān” de píngguǒ gēn “dàjídàlì” de júzi.
text.english: Also, we still have apples symbolizing peace, and tangerines symbolizing great fortune and great favor.

text.traditional: 我了解了，真是又特別又豐富的大餐！
text.simplified: 我了解了，真是又特别又丰富的大餐！
text.pinyin: Wǒ liǎojiě le, zhēnshì yòu tèbié yòu fēngfù de dà cān!
text.english: I get it. It is really a special and abundant meal!

text.traditional: 如果你跟我去爺爺奶奶家過年，今年的除夕就更加熱鬧了！
text.simplified: 如果你跟我去爷爷奶奶家过年，今年的除夕就更加热闹了！
text.pinyin: Rúguǒ nǐ gēn wǒ qù yéye nǎinai jiā guònián, jīnnián de chúxī jiù gèngjiā rènao le!
text.english: If you go to my grandparents’ house with me, this Chinese New Year’s Eve will be even more lively!

text.traditional: （這個時候，以凡的手機響了，是媽媽寄給他的一封電子郵件，他看完以後很難過。）
text.simplified: （这个时候，以凡的手机响了，是妈妈寄给他的一封电子邮件，他看完以后很难过。）
text.pinyin: (Zhège shíhòu, Yǐfán de shǒujī xiǎng le, shì māma jì gěi tā de yì fēng diànzǐ yóujiàn, tā kàn wán yǐhòu hěn nánguò.)
text.english: (At that moment Yifan’s cellphone rang. It was his mom sending him an email. He was very sad after reading it.)

text.traditional: 我媽媽說，她訂不到機票，寒假不能來看我了。
text.simplified: 我妈妈说，她订不到机票，寒假不能来看我了。
text.pinyin: Wǒ māma shuō, tā dìng búdào jīpiào, hánjià bùnéng lái kàn wǒ le.
text.english: My mom said that she couldn’t book the ticket so that she couldn’t come to see me during winter vacation.

text.traditional: 沒關係，等過完年，我帶你去找我舅舅、舅媽，他們很親切，而且舅媽會做義大利麵，你可以吃吃看。
text.simplified: 没关系，等过完年，我带你去找我舅舅、舅妈，他们很亲切，而且舅妈会做义大利面，你可以吃吃看。
text.pinyin: Méiguānxi, děng guò wán nián, wǒ dài nǐ qù zhǎo wǒ jiùjiu, jiùmā, tāmen hěn qīnqiè, érqiě jiùmā huì zuò Yìdàlì miàn, nǐ kěyǐ chīchi kàn.
text.english: It’s ok. After the Chinese New Year, I’ll take you to visit my uncle and aunt. They are very kind to people. Besides, my aunt can make pasta. You can try it.

text.traditional: （心裡感覺相當溫暖）好啊！太感謝妳了！
text.simplified: （心里感觉相当温暖）好啊！太感谢你了！
text.pinyin: (Xīnlǐ gǎnjué xiāngdāng wēnnuǎn) Hǎo a! Tài gǎnxiè nǐ le!
text.english: (Feels quite warm inside.) Alright! Thank you so much!

text.traditional: 對了！元宵節那天，我可以帶你去看燈會，有的燈籠上面還畫了十二生肖。
text.simplified: 对了！元宵节那天，我可以带你去看灯会，有的灯笼上面还画了十二生肖。
text.pinyin: Duìle! Yuánxiāojié nà tiān, wǒ kěyǐ dài nǐ qù kàn dēnghuì, yǒude dēnglóng shàngmiàn hái huà le shí'èr shēngxiào.
text.english: Oh! On Lantern Festival, I can take you to the lantern show. There are also zodiac paintings on some of the lanterns.

text.traditional: 十二生肖？
text.simplified: 十二生肖？
text.pinyin: Shí'èr shēngxiào?
text.english: Zodiac?

text.traditional: 對啊！就是鼠、牛、虎、兔、龍、蛇、馬、羊、猴、雞、狗、豬。
text.simplified: 对啊！就是鼠、牛、虎、兔、龙、蛇、马、羊、猴、鸡、狗、猪。
text.pinyin: Duì a! Jiùshì shǔ, niú, hǔ, tù, lóng, shé, mǎ, yáng, hóu, jī, gǒu, zhū.
text.english: Right! It is the mouse, the cow, the tiger, the rabbit, the dragon, the snake, the horse, the sheep, the monkey, the chicken, the dog, and the pig.

text.traditional: 妳說了這麼多動物，怎麼沒有貓呢？
text.simplified: 你说了这么多动物，怎么没有猫呢？
text.pinyin: Nǐ shuō le zhème duō dòngwù, zěnme méiyǒu māo ne?
text.english: You mentioned so many animals. Why are there no cats?

text.traditional: 有空我們再告訴你十二生肖的故事。你不知道我是屬虎的吧？
text.simplified: 有空我们再告诉你十二生肖的故事。你不知道我是属虎的吧？
text.pinyin: Yǒukòng wǒmen zài gàosu nǐ shí'èr shēngxiào de gùshì. Nǐ bù zhīdào wǒ shì shǔ hǔ de ba?
text.english: When we have time, we will tell you the story of the zodiac. You don’t know that I was born in the year of the tiger?

text.traditional: 是嗎？難怪妳那麼愛生氣！
text.simplified: 是吗？难怪你那么爱生气！
text.pinyin: Shì ma? Nánguài nǐ nàme ài shēngqì!
text.english: Were you? No wonder you enjoy getting angry so much!

text.traditional: 哈哈哈……
text.simplified: 哈哈哈……
text.pinyin: Hāhāhā…
text.english: Hahaha...

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Link a situation with the result that follows right away.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern indicates when a situation occurs, another situation ensues right away. In this pattern, “當” is often followed by “……的時候”.
grammarPages.pattern: 當 + situation（+ 的時候），就 + result

text.traditional: 當警察一出現，小偷就趕快跑了。
text.simplified: 当警察一出现，小偷就赶快跑了。
text.pinyin: Dāng jǐngchá yì chūxiàn, xiǎotōu jiù gǎnkuài pǎo le.
text.english: As soon as the police appeared, the thief ran away quickly.

text.traditional: 當你覺得難過、生氣的時候，就應該去操場運動一下。
text.simplified: 当你觉得难过、生气的时候，就应该去操场运动一下。
text.pinyin: Dāng nǐ juéde nánguò, shēngqì de shíhòu, jiù yīnggāi qù cāochǎng yùndòng yíxià.
text.english: When you feel sad or angry, you should go exercise on the sports field.

text.traditional: 當莫以凡第一天參加功夫社的時候，就愛上了中國功夫。
text.simplified: 当莫以凡第一天参加功夫社的时候，就爱上了中国功夫。
text.pinyin: Dāng Mò Yǐfán dìyī tiān cānjiā gōngfu shè de shíhòu, jiù àishàng le Zhōngguó gōngfu.
text.english: On his very first day at the kungfu club, Mo Yifan fell in love with Chinese kungfu.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 當……，就…….
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Answer each question with 當……，就…….

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 讓 as a passive marker or as a verb meaning cause, allow, or let.
grammarPages.explanation: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: 1. Used as Preposition: S＋讓＋NP（＋給）＋V了 This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be. 2. Used as Verb: (1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen (2) to allow, to permit someone to do something (3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.
grammarPages.pattern: S + 讓 + NP（+ 給）+ V了

text.traditional: 李先生剛買的照相機讓同事（給）弄壞了。
text.simplified: 李先生刚买的照相机让同事（给）弄坏了。
text.pinyin: Lǐ xiānshēng gāng mǎi de zhàoxiàngjī ràng tóngshì (gěi) nòng huài le.
text.english: The camera Mr. Li just bought was broken by a coworker.

text.traditional: 每次跟朋友去 KTV 唱歌，都讓他非常開心。
text.simplified: 每次跟朋友去 KTV 唱歌，都让他非常开心。
text.pinyin: Měicì gēn péngyǒu qù KTV chànggē, dōu ràng tā fēicháng kāixīn.
text.english: Every time he goes to KTV to sing with friends, it makes him very happy.

text.traditional: 我不舒服，老師讓我早一點兒回家休息。
text.simplified: 我不舒服，老师让我早一点儿回家休息。
text.pinyin: Wǒ bù shūfu, lǎoshī ràng wǒ zǎo yìdiǎnr huí jiā xiūxí.
text.english: I didn’t feel well, so the teacher let me go home early to rest.

text.traditional: 媽媽讓孩子把臥室打掃好了以後，才能玩遊戲。
text.simplified: 妈妈让孩子把卧室打扫好了以后，才能玩游戏。
text.pinyin: Māma ràng háizi bǎ wòshì dǎsǎo hǎo le yǐhòu, cáinéng wán yóuxì.
text.english: Mom had the child finish cleaning the bedroom first; only then could the child play games.

text.traditional: 老闆讓我留下來把筆電修好，才讓我下班。這件事讓我很生氣。
text.simplified: 老板让我留下来把笔电修好，才让我下班。这件事让我很生气。
text.pinyin: Lǎobǎn ràng wǒ liú xià lái bǎ bǐdiàn xiū hǎo, cái ràng wǒ xiàbān. Zhè jiàn shì ràng wǒ hěn shēngqì.
text.english: The boss made me stay and fix the laptop, and only then let me leave work. This made me very angry.

subsections.title: Used as Preposition
subsections.explanation: This pattern functions as the passive voice expression. The usage of “讓” here is similar to “被”; however, the Agent after “被” can be omitted while after “讓” cannot be.
subsections.pattern: S + 讓 + NP（+ 給）+ V了

subsections.title: Used as Verb
subsections.explanation:
(1) to make someone ..., to cause something to happen
(2) to allow, to permit someone to do something
(3) to let someone do something or to have someone do something: This usage of imperative “讓” is more polite and euphemistic.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Say that a choice or situation does not matter to someone.
grammarPages.explanation: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: This pattern is often placed after the things the speaker feels indifferent to or does not care about. It can also be used independently.

text.traditional: 父母覺得孩子胖或是瘦都無所謂，只要健康就好了。
text.simplified: 父母觉得孩子胖或是瘦都无所谓，只要健康就好了。
text.pinyin: Fùmǔ juéde háizi pàng huòshì shòu dōu wúsuǒwèi, zhǐyào jiànkāng jiù hǎo le.
text.english: The parents don’t mind whether their child is fat or thin, as long as the child is healthy.

text.traditional: 太太：這個週末我們要去哪裡玩？先生：妳決定吧！我無所謂。
text.simplified: 太太：这个周末我们要去哪里玩？先生：你决定吧！我无所谓。
text.pinyin: Tàitai: Zhège zhōumò wǒmen yào qù nǎlǐ wán? Xiānshēng: Nǐ juédìng ba! Wǒ wúsuǒwèi.
text.english: Wife: Where should we go this weekend? Husband: You decide! I don’t mind.

text.traditional: 老闆：歡迎你來我的餐廳打工，可是錢不多，你願意嗎？學生：錢多不多無所謂，只要能得到寶貴的經驗就好了。
text.simplified: 老板：欢迎你来我的餐厅打工，可是钱不多，你愿意吗？学生：钱多不多无所谓，只要能得到宝贵的经验就好了。
text.pinyin: Lǎobǎn: Huānyíng nǐ lái wǒ de cāntīng dǎgōng, kěshì qián bù duō, nǐ yuànyì ma? Xuéshēng: Qián duō bù duō wúsuǒwèi, zhǐyào néng dédào bǎoguì de jīngyàn jiù hǎo le.
text.english: Boss: Welcome to work at my restaurant, but the pay is low. Are you willing? Student: Whether the pay is high or low doesn’t matter, as long as I can gain valuable experience.

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete each response with 無所謂.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Use 走 after a verb to show that something leaves or disappears, or that an action can or cannot make it leave.
grammarPages.explanation: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: In this pattern, V can be action verbs, such as “搬（move）”, “拿（take）”, “帶（bring）”, “跑（run）”, “趕（drive）”, “嚇（scare）”, etc. “走” means “to go” or “to leave”. The “走” after the verb, used as post verb complement, means to leave or to disappear.
grammarPages.pattern: V + 走了／沒 + V + 走／V + 得走／V + 不走

text.traditional: 你們說話的聲音太大了，把孩子們都嚇走了。
text.simplified: 你们说话的声音太大了，把孩子们都吓走了。
text.pinyin: Nǐmen shuōhuà de shēngyīn tài dà le, bǎ háizi men dōu xià zǒu le.
text.english: Your voices were so loud that you scared the children away.

text.traditional: 良介已經不住在宿舍了，他上個學期末就搬走了。
text.simplified: 良介已经不住在宿舍了，他上个学期末就搬走了。
text.pinyin: Liángjiè yǐjīng bú zhù zài sùshè le, tā shàng ge xuéqí mò jiù bān zǒu le.
text.english: Ryosuke no longer lives in the dorm; he moved out at the end of last semester.

text.traditional: 這些小說是她要送給同學的，所以回國的時候沒帶走。
text.simplified: 这些小说是她要送给同学的，所以回国的时候没带走。
text.pinyin: Zhèxiē xiǎoshuō shì tā yào sòng gěi tóngxué de, suǒyǐ huíguó de shíhòu méi dài zǒu.
text.english: These novels are for her classmates, so she didn’t take them with her when she returned home.

text.traditional: 把錢存在銀行很安全，誰偷得走呢？
text.simplified: 把钱存在银行很安全，谁偷得走呢？
text.pinyin: Bǎ qián cúnzài yínháng hěn ānquán, shéi tōu de zǒu ne?
text.english: It’s safe to keep money in the bank. Who could steal it?

text.traditional: 有一隻蟲子飛進我的房間裡，怎麼趕都趕不走。
text.simplified: 有一只虫子飞进我的房间里，怎么赶都赶不走。
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì zhī chóngzi fēi jìn wǒ de fángjiān lǐ, zěnme gǎn dōu gǎn bù zǒu.
text.english: A bug flew into my room, and no matter how I shoo it, I can’t get it to leave.

grammarPages.lessonTitleEnglish: Fish on the Dish, Abundance Year after Year
grammarPages.learnerPromise: Name an accomplished fact that prevented a different situation from happening.
grammarPages.explanation: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.explanationEnglish: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.sourceExplanationEnglish: “要不是” is followed by an accomplished fact. Without the fact, a following situation would occur. That is, the following situation did not really occur.
grammarPages.pattern: 要不是 + accomplished fact，result that would otherwise occur

text.traditional: 要不是春假去了阿里山，我就看不到那麼美麗的日出了。
text.simplified: 要不是春假去了阿里山，我就看不到那么美丽的日出了。
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì chūnjià qù le Ālǐ Shān, wǒ jiù kàn búdào nàme měilì de rìchū le.
text.english: If I hadn’t gone to Alishan during spring break, I wouldn’t have seen such a beautiful sunrise.

text.traditional: 要不是去同學家過年，莫以凡一個人在宿舍一定會很無聊的。
text.simplified: 要不是去同学家过年，莫以凡一个人在宿舍一定会很无聊的。
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì qù tóngxué jiā guònián, Mò Yǐfán yígerén zài sùshè yídìng huì hěn wúliáo de.
text.english: If he hadn’t gone to a classmate’s home for New Year, Mo Yifan would have been very bored alone in the dorm.

text.traditional: 要不是住過民宿，我就不知道有些民宿比飯店更舒服呢！
text.simplified: 要不是住过民宿，我就不知道有些民宿比饭店更舒服呢！
text.pinyin: Yàobúshì zhù guo mínsù, wǒ jiù bù zhīdào yǒuxiē mínsù bǐ fàndiàn gèng shūfu ne!
text.english: If I hadn’t stayed at a homestay, I wouldn’t know that some homestays are more comfortable than hotels!

grammarPages.exercisePreview: Complete the dialogues with 要不是.
grammarPages.exerciseInstruction: Complete the dialogues with 要不是.

text.traditional: 從前，有一隻住在海裡的怪獸，名字叫「年」。從一月到十二月，「年」都在睡覺，什麼東西都不吃。到了除夕，當天一黑，「年」就會出來找東西吃。雞、鴨、人等動物，「年」都吃，讓大家非常害怕，不能好好地過日子，只好帶著一些食物，趕快跑到山上去。
text.simplified: 从前，有一只住在海里的怪兽，名字叫「年」。从一月到十二月，「年」都在睡觉，什么东西都不吃。到了除夕，当天一黑，「年」就会出来找东西吃。鸡、鸭、人等动物，「年」都吃，让大家非常害怕，不能好好地过日子，只好带着一些食物，赶快跑到山上去。
text.pinyin: Cóngqián, yǒu yì zhī zhù zài hǎi lǐ de guàishòu, míngzi jiào “nián”. Cóng yī yuè dào shí'èr yuè, “nián” dōu zài shuìjiào, shénme dōngxi dōu bù chī. Dào le chúxī, dāngtiān yì hēi, “nián” jiù huì chūlái zhǎo dōngxi chī. Jī, yā, rén děng dòngwù, “nián” dōu chī, ràng dàjiā fēicháng hàipà, bùnéng hǎohǎo de guòrìzi, zhǐhǎo dài zhe yìxiē shíwù, gǎnkuài pǎo dào shān shàngqù.
text.english: Once upon a time, there was a monster living in the sea. It was called “Nian”. Nian slept all the time from January to December without eating anything. On the Chinese New Year’s Eve, as soon as the sky went dark, Nian went out to search for food. Nian ate animals, such as chickens, ducks, people, and so on. This made everyone very frightened and unable to live a normal life. They had no choice but to take some food and rush to the mountains.

text.traditional: 有一年除夕，一個老太太和她先生不願意離開家。他們家很窮，只有一點米，什麼食物都沒有。而且老太太覺得他們家只有兩口人，年紀都大了，讓怪獸給吃了也無所謂。
text.simplified: 有一年除夕，一个老太太和她先生不愿意离开家。他们家很穷，只有一点米，什么食物都没有。而且老太太觉得他们家只有两口人，年纪都大了，让怪兽给吃了也无所谓。
text.pinyin: Yǒu yì nián chúxī, yíge lǎotàitai hé tā xiānshēng bú yuànyì líkāi jiā. Tāmen jiā hěn qióng, zhǐyǒu yìdiǎn mǐ, shénme shíwù dōu méiyǒu. Érqiě lǎotàitai juéde tāmen jiā zhǐyǒu liǎng kǒu rén, niánjì dōu dà le, ràng guàishòu gěi chī le yě wúsuǒwèi.
text.english: On one Chinese New Year’s Eve, an old lady and her husband didn’t want to leave their home. They were very poor. They had no food except for a little rice. Furthermore, the old lady thought there were only two people in the family, and both were in old age, so they did not care if they were eaten.

text.traditional: 那天下午，老太太的家門口忽然出現了一個老人，他請老太太分一點東西給他吃。老太太覺得他很可憐，就煮了一點兒飯請他吃。老人一邊吃，一邊跟老太太說：「妳不用怕『年』，只要準備幾張紅紙、一些竹子，就可以把『年』趕走了。」
text.simplified: 那天下午，老太太的家门口忽然出现了一个老人，他请老太太分一点东西给他吃。老太太觉得他很可怜，就煮了一点儿饭请他吃。老人一边吃，一边跟老太太说：「你不用怕『年』，只要准备几张红纸、一些竹子，就可以把『年』赶走了。」
text.pinyin: Nà tiān xiàwǔ, lǎotàitai de jiā ménkǒu hūrán chūxiàn le yíge lǎorén, tā qǐng lǎotàitai fēn yìdiǎn dōngxi gěi tā chī. Lǎotàitai juéde tā hěn kělián, jiù zhǔ le yìdiǎnr fàn qǐng tā chī. Lǎorén yìbiān chī, yìbiān gēn lǎotàitai shuō: “Nǐ búyòng pà “nián”, zhǐyào zhǔnbèi jǐ zhāng hóng zhǐ, yìxiē zhúzi, jiù kěyǐ bǎ “nián” gǎn zǒu le.”
text.english: That afternoon, an old man appeared suddenly in front of their house door. He asked the old lady to give him something to eat. The old lady thought he was very pitiful, so she cooked a little rice for him. While the old man was eating, he said: “You don’t need to be afraid of Nian. As long as you prepare a few sheets of red paper and some bamboo, you can drive it away.”

text.traditional: 天剛黑，「年」就真的來了。「年」看見了門上的紅紙、地上燒竹子的火，又聽見燒竹子的時候大大的聲音，就嚇得跑走了。原來，「年」怕的就是：紅色、亮亮的東西和很大的聲音。
text.simplified: 天刚黑，「年」就真的来了。「年」看见了门上的红纸、地上烧竹子的火，又听见烧竹子的时候大大的声音，就吓得跑走了。原来，「年」怕的就是：红色、亮亮的东西和很大的声音。
text.pinyin: Tiān gāng hēi, “nián” jiù zhēnde lái le. “Nián” kànjiàn le mén shàng de hóng zhǐ, dì shàng shāo zhúzi de huǒ, yòu tīngjiàn shāo zhúzi de shíhòu dàdà de shēngyīn, jiù xià de pǎo zǒu le. Yuánlái, “nián” pà de jiùshì: hóngsè, liàng liàng de dōngxi hé hěn dà de shēngyīn.
text.english: When the sky just got dark, Nian did come. As soon as Nian saw the red paper at the door, a fire that burned bamboo on the ground, and heard the loud sound made by the burning bamboo, it became so scared that it ran away. It turned out that Nian was afraid of red, bright things and loud sounds.

text.traditional: 第二天，大家從山上回來時，發現老太太和她先生沒被「年」吃了，都覺得很奇怪。老太太說，要不是老人告訴她把「年」嚇走的方法，他們就被吃了。
text.simplified: 第二天，大家从山上回来时，发现老太太和她先生没被「年」吃了，都觉得很奇怪。老太太说，要不是老人告诉她把「年」吓走的方法，他们就被吃了。
text.pinyin: Dì'èr tiān, dàjiā cóng shān shàng huílái shí, fāxiàn lǎotàitai hé tā xiānshēng méi bèi “nián” chī le, dōu juéde hěn qíguài. Lǎotàitai shuō, yàobúshì lǎorén gàosu tā bǎ “nián” xià zǒu de fāngfǎ, tāmen jiù bèi chī le.
text.english: The next day, everybody came back from the mountains and found it strange that the old lady and her husband were not eaten by Nian. The old lady said that if the old man hadn’t told her how to scare Nian away, they would have been eaten.

text.traditional: 從那個時候起，每年的除夕，大家都會在門口貼紅紙、燒竹子。這就是為什麼中國人在過年的時候，要貼春聯、放鞭炮了。
text.simplified: 从那个时候起，每年的除夕，大家都会在门口贴红纸、烧竹子。这就是为什么中国人在过年的时候，要贴春联、放鞭炮了。
text.pinyin: Cóng nà ge shíhòu qǐ, měi nián de chúxī, dàjiā dōu huì zài ménkǒu tiē hóng zhǐ, shāo zhúzi. Zhè jiù shì wèishénme Zhōngguó rén zài guònián de shíhòu, yào tiē chūnlián, fàng biānpào le.
text.english: From then on, every Chinese New Year’s Eve, everyone pastes red paper on their door and burns bamboo. This is also the very reason why the Chinese paste spring couplets and set off firecrackers during the Chinese New Year.
